comments.note: src/config/config.ts line 220: the per-field length validation calls .trim() before the > maxLen check, meaning it validates the trimmed length rather than the raw length. WP-002 spec states 'trimming must occur after length validation to preserve the current validation semantics (validate raw values, then trim)'. Practical impact is negligible given the generous limits (100–500 chars), but it diverges from the documented contract. A value padded with whitespace to exceed the raw limit (e.g. 101 leading spaces + content) would silently pass length validation. Recommend aligning with spec in a follow-up.

src/config/config.ts legacy-format branch (line 284): label is set to the raw host key string (not trimmed), while host is trimmed (line 285). This creates a subtle asymmetry where entry.label may contain leading/trailing whitespace that entry.host does not. AC2 only requires host and token to be trimmed for legacy format, so this is spec-compliant, but downstream consumers that display label without trimming will see the inconsistency.

Developer handoff note claimed 'the current implementation validates raw values first, then trims' but inspection of line 220 shows the length check uses the trimmed value. No correctness bug given the limits, but the handoff note is misleading for the next reviewer.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (src/config/config.ts, src/tests/config.test.ts). Change scope: trim-on-parse for GitCredentialEntry fields in parseGitCredentials(). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 1 Low / 1 Info observation recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: No security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed; no Critical or High issues identified. Full review summary below.

A01 (Broken Access Control): Not applicable to this change. parseGitCredentials() is a pure parsing helper with no access control responsibility. The credential resolution logic in git-credentials.ts (resolveCredential / injectCredentialToken) is unmodified and already documented with the known host/credentialId coherence caveat. No new access control surface introduced.

A02 (Cryptographic Failures): Tokens are PATs stored as plaintext in config.json (pre-existing design). The existing saveConfigField() already applies chmod 0o600 on POSIX systems. The trim-on-parse change does not affect storage format or transport. Tokens are correctly masked in API responses via maskToken() (last 4 chars only). No new cryptographic risk introduced by this change.

A03 (Injection): Token values are injected into HTTPS URLs via WHATWG URL.username assignment (injectCredentialToken, git-credentials.ts line 112), which percent-encodes special characters automatically — no string concatenation is used. Trimming normalises leading/trailing whitespace before this path, which reduces rather than increases injection surface. No injection risk introduced.

A04 (Insecure Design): The trim order vs. length-check order divergence (config.ts line 220 trims before the > maxLen check) was flagged by QA. Security assessment: with limits of 100–500 characters, a whitespace-padded value that would exceed the raw limit but pass the trimmed-length check is an edge case with negligible practical impact — no credential value in normal use would be padded with >100 leading spaces. This is a spec compliance gap, not a security vulnerability. Recommend aligning with spec in a follow-up work package.

A05 (Security Misconfiguration): No new configuration surface. Validation error messages in parseGitCredentials() reference field names and index positions but do not leak sensitive values (token content is never included in error strings). No misconfiguration risk introduced.
A06 (Vulnerable & Outdated Components): No new dependencies introduced by this change. The implementation uses only built-in JavaScript string methods (.trim(), .map()). No CVE risk.

A07 (Identification & Authentication Failures): Not directly applicable — this is config parsing, not an auth endpoint. The downstream consumer (git-credentials.ts) is unmodified. Trimming normalises token values at load time, ensuring consistent lookup by credential ID. No auth regression.
A08 (Software & Data Integrity Failures): No deserialization, no build artifact change. The .map() final pass returns a new typed array — no prototype pollution risk. No integrity risk introduced.

A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures): The audit logging in server/routes/config.ts (credential create / update / delete) is unmodified. Token values are explicitly excluded from audit log entries. The trim-on-parse change does not affect audit trail behaviour. No logging regression.

A10 (SSRF): The host field is used downstream to match a GitCredentialEntry against a repository URL's hostname (resolveCredential, git-credentials.ts line 86: c.host === host, where host is extracted via WHATWG URL parsing). Trimming normalises the stored host value. No SSRF vector introduced — the host field is not used to initiate outbound requests directly; it is only used for credential matching. The actual URL used for git operations originates from repository config, not from the credential host field.

INFO — Spec alignment gap (trim-before-length-check): config.ts line 220 performs (entry[field] as string).trim() before the > maxLen check. The WP-002 spec intended raw-value length to be validated first, then trim applied. No exploitable security risk given the generous limits (100–500 chars), but diverges from the documented contract. Log for follow-up; no security blocking impact.
